results.title: AgentGrid.io (by Anima) MCP Server: Tools, Setup & Config
results.content:
## Example prompts

 "Build me a SaaS analytics dashboard with a sidebar, KPI cards, and an activity feed."
 "Clone stripe.com/payments into an app."
 "Turn this Figma frame into a working site: ..."
 "The header on this artifact is broken on mobile, fix it."
 "Implement this Figma design in my project."
 "Publish it."

## Best practices

Describe intent, not CSS. AgentGrid.io is design-aware. Say what it's for, who it's for, and the 3 to 5 features that matter, rather than hex values and pixel sizes.

Be specific when implementing. "Implement the login form using our existing Button and Input components from `src/components/ui`" beats "implement this design".

Break down large designs. Header first, then the card grid, then the footer.

## Troubleshooting [...] agent, and another may be working the same one. A comment addressed to PEOPLE and not to you never reaches you at all. A comment may name several parties, agents and people together. `alsoAsked` lists everyone else it names, so you can see a colleague is on it and not redo their work. Any of them may resolve it, and resolving closes it FOR ALL OF THEM. The mentions in the body may scope parts of the request — "@you fix the header, @someone else the footer" — and that scoping is in the words, not in the fields. So when you have done only your part, REPLY rather than resolve: resolving would close the others' half too, and they would never learn it was dropped. A comment may point at nothing in particular — that is the reviewer's note about the artifact as a whole, and it carries no anchor. [...] Say something back on ONE review comment and LEAVE IT OPEN — to ask what the reviewer meant, to report what you found, or to say you are blocked. Use this rather than review-resolve whenever the exchange is not finished: resolving closes it, and the reviewer would have to open a new comment to answer you. The reviewer sees your message in the artifact, and their answer comes back on the same comment — call review-list again to read it. They may not reply immediately, so do not wait on it. You may reply to a comment addressed to you, or to one marked `unassigned`. A closed comment takes no more replies — it answers replied: false, because nobody is reading that thread any more. results.title: The new handoff: How to share your AI agent's code with your team - Anima Blog
results.content:
Instead of writing a separate Slack message explaining which component is broken, they can leave feedback attached to the relevant part of the artifact.

AgentGrid supports review comments on app elements and document passages. Authorized people and agents can work through those comments together.

That keeps the discussion close to the thing being reviewed.

### Step 5: Let the agent continue the work

Now you can tell a connected agent:

Open this AgentGrid artifact and fix the date filter. Keep the existing layout and update the same artifact.

Include the actual artifact URL.

The agent can inspect and update the artifact if it has the required access and capabilities.
